name: stlink
why: Flashes and debugs STM32 boards over USB, a real door into hardware if you own a discovery board.

brief.what_it_is: stlink is an open source toolset for programming and debugging STM32 microcontrollers and boards from STMicroelectronics. It talks to ST-LINK programmer hardware (the onboard debugger on Discovery and Nucleo boards, or a standalone probe) over USB, translating commands to JTAG or SWD. The toolset includes st-info (chip and programmer info), st-flash (flash manipulation), st-trace (execution logging), st-server (serves a local ST-LINK over TCP), and st-util (a GDB server). It also ships stlink-lib, a communication library, and an optional stlink-gui.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as an open source alternative to ST's own STLINK tools, covering all four generations of ST-LINK programmer boards and clones. It says there is no difference in handling between the revisions at the user level.
brief.how_it_works: Each ST-LINK generation uses a microcontroller on the probe to translate USB commands into JTAG/SWD. The V1 uses SCSI passthru over USB, while V2, V2-1 and V3 use raw USB commands. The st-util tool acts as a GDB server, which the README says works with VS Code or VSCodium through the Cortex-Debug plugin.
brief.install_notes: On Linux, the README recommends installing stlink-tools from your distribution's package repository, and lists Arch, Alpine, Fedora and FreeBSD packages. For Debian or Ubuntu it points to the project's own deb package on the GitHub releases page, which it prefers over the distro packages. On Windows, stand-alone binaries come in i686 and x86_64 zip archives from release v1.6.1 onward, and they can be unzipped anywhere. On macOS there are no binaries, so you must compile from source using doc/compiling.md. The README lists no accounts, runtimes or first-run steps.
brief.standout: It covers every ST-LINK generation, including the obsolete V1, under one toolset, and it doubles as a GDB server for VS Code via Cortex-Debug. Its st-server mode serves a local probe over TCP, so remote tools can use it.
brief.status: Maintained, with weak evidence. The README badges show CI, CodeQL and commit activity on the develop branch, and a commits-since-v1.9.0 counter. I did not see a release date or a last-commit date, so I could not confirm recency.
brief.caveats: macOS users must compile from source, and no binaries are provided. Windows builds are tested only through CI. The STLINK/V1 is marked obsolete as of 21-11-2019, though it is still supported. The README says the Debian and Ubuntu packages differ from the project's own deb. Licensing is BSD-3. The README points to supported_devices.md for the list of working MCU targets, which I did not open.
quotes: stlink is an open source toolset to program and debug STM32 devices and boards manufactured by STMicroelectronics.
On the user level there is no difference in handling or operation between these different revisions.
The stlink library and tools are licensed under the BSD-3 License.
